chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, on the authority of Abi Himmam - Isma'il ibn Himmam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them both)

That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Above every good deed is a good deed, until a man is killed in the way of Allah, the Almighty. Once he is killed in the way of Allah, there is no deed higher than it. Above every act of disobedience is disobedience, until a man kills one of his parents. Once he kills one of them, there is no act of disobedience greater than it.'

key_terms.بِرّ: Goodness or piety (a general term for virtuous deeds)
key_terms.عُقُوق: Disobedience or impious conduct, specifically towards parents
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: In the way of Allah (often referring to jihad or martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: What is the highest good deed and the worst act of disobedience according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes a comparative hierarchy of virtues and vices, highlighting martyrdom as the supreme good and parental homicide as the ultimate evil. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that while martyrdom is the highest rank, it does not negate the cumulative merit of other good deeds, whereas killing a parent represents the peak of 'uquq' (disobiance) from which there is no higher degree of wickedness. The narration underscores the unique status of the parents in Islamic ethics, linking their rights directly to the magnitude of the sin incurred by their murder.
